title: I text my AI agent and it edits my reels (AGENT-16 carousel, 76-hermes-edits-reels-house)
summary: Metricool: scheduled Fri 30 Oct 13:00 IG + TikTok
body: Metricool: scheduled Fri 30 Oct 13:00 IG + TikTok
guide: Turn a chat message into an edited reel: you send raw clips and a short instruction to an AI agent, and it cuts, captions and returns a finished video. You need ChatGPT (Codex) or Claude Code, a Telegram bot, ffmpeg, and Google Drive.
1. Create a Telegram bot with BotFather and keep its token in an environment variable, not in your code.
1. Ask ChatGPT (Codex) or Claude Code to write a small script that listens to that bot and saves any video you send into a Google Drive folder.
1. Have the same script pass your text instruction and the saved clip to an AI agent, such as Claude Code run from the command line or an open-source agent framework.
1. Give the agent ffmpeg and tell it the edit steps: trim dead air, join the best takes, burn in captions, and export a vertical 9:16 file.
1. Let the agent send a short preview back to you in the Telegram chat before anything is final.
1. Reply with changes in plain English, and have the agent re-render and send the new version.
1. Finish in CapCut if you want extra polish, then schedule the post in Metricool.
Watch out: only let the bot answer your own Telegram account, and never auto-publish without a preview you have approved.

```
You are helping me build a Telegram-controlled video editing assistant. I use <my operating system> and have <ChatGPT Codex or Claude Code>, Python, ffmpeg, a Google Drive account and a Telegram bot token from BotFather.
Build a script that does the following:
1. Listens to my Telegram bot, but only accepts messages from my own user ID, <my Telegram user ID>.
2. Saves any video I send to a Google Drive folder called <folder name>.
3. Reads my text instruction, for example "cut the pauses and add captions".
4. Calls an AI agent to plan the edit, then runs ffmpeg to trim silences, join the chosen takes, burn in captions and export a 9:16 MP4.
5. Sends a short preview back to me in Telegram and waits for my reply.
6. If I reply with changes, re-renders and sends the new version, keeping the old one.
Constraints: read all tokens and keys from environment variables, never publish anything automatically, and log each step in plain language so I can see what happened.
Return the full code, a list of the packages to install, the exact setup steps for the Telegram bot and Google Drive access, and a short test I can run with one sample clip.
```
